headline: The brief's premise is STALE: touch IS wired (main.js -> engine.js -> input/real.js:19 -> touch.js) and real CDP touch events reach it at HEAD. The work is now proving a phone can PLAY.
findings: F1 (CORRECTS THE DISPATCH). `game/src/main.js` does not import touch.js and never needed to. The chain is main.js -> Engine (engine.js:57 imports RealInput) -> input/real.js:19 `import { TouchInput }` -> constructed at real.js:73, attached by `applyDeviceClass('handheld')` at real.js:405, ticked inside the FIXED STEP by sim/step.js:69 -> real.js:466. `git log -S 'import { TouchInput }'` dates the import to 6eb8f04. Grepping main.js for 'touch' proves nothing about whether touch is wired.

F2 (MEASURED, not argued). A phone-shaped Playwright context (844x390, dpr 3, hasTouch, isMobile, webdriver spoofed false) boots into mode 'play' with an empty query string, reports deviceClass 'handheld', touchState().shown === true, 11 controls laid out, 0 inset violations. A REAL CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` at (200,300) opens a floating stick with origin exactly (200,300); a touchMove to (260,260) gives stick {x:0.667,y:0.444}; touchEnd clears it. Screenshot shows the arc drawn on the title screen.

F3. docs/play/ is IN SYNC with game/ (`node tools/publish-game.mjs --check` -> 710 files match), so the published copy the owner's phone loads has the same touch path. The 'phone gets no controls at all' symptom is not reproducible at 9a3e1a7.

F4 (REAL, and fixed by me). T5 was kept by TWO copies of one line: gamepad.js `_applyButtons` and touch.js `tick` each computed `(frame - pressFrame + 1) >= (gate.frames || 12)`. RULES 10. Extracted to `game/src/input/hold-gate.js`; both now call `shouldPromote()`. To be proved by breaking that one file on a copy of the tree and watching BOTH arms go red together.

rulings.question: What does touch do for name entry, given a full-screen keyboard panel is forbidden by RI-JRN01 O8?
rulings.decision: REUSE THE PAD'S ANSWER UNCHANGED — pick from the ledger. No touch-specific code at all.
rulings.why: character/scene.js `_nameOptions()` already turns every text node (hold.hatch-name, writ.given-name, writ.class-custom-name) into a pick list, and `CensusSurface.step(input)` moves the caret on `input.moveY` and commits on `pressedName('interact')`. Both are DEVICE-NEUTRAL action-layer reads. The touch stick writes moveY through `pipe.setMove` and the arc's `interact` button writes the edge. So the ledger is reachable on touch with zero new code, and the semantics a player learns on a pad transfer exactly, which is T5's whole argument applied to a menu.
rulings.rule: RULES 0 — decided and recorded, not asked
rulings.reversible_if: play-testing shows players want a name the ledger does not carry. Then the owed thing is an INLINE (never full-screen, O8) character wheel driven by the same moveY/interact pair — not an OS keyboard, which would also cover the whole lower half of a landscape phone with the controls on it.
